clue.text: Notice nothing, with crack going up temple

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from the bottom of the column, so backwards

blocks.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement
the figure zero
a crack or opening

explanation.surface: Someone climbing a temple wall fails to spot a crack as they go up.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower built as a Buddhist or Hindu temple in East Asia.

clue.text: Item used for cleaning wicket remains on pitch for cricket

blocks.note: W is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a wicket
ash is what remains after burning
to bowl is to pitch the ball in cricket; 'on' places this piece after the others

explanation.surface: A groundsman's cleaning gear and the debris left on a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler delivers, or pitches, the ball, so 'pitch for cricket' is the verb BOWL rather than the playing strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A washbowl is a basin that holds water for washing hands and face, so it is equipment for cleaning.

clue.text: Fraud investigator gets crumby food

blocks.note: a scam is a fraud
PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A detective looking into fraud tucks into a meal that leaves crumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are langoustine tails usually served coated in breadcrumbs and fried, hence crumby food.

clue.text: Expert in male grooming has no hesitation making jibe

indicators.note: the expert is left without the hesitation sound, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: a barber cuts and shaves men's hair
the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A barber who speaks without hesitating delivers a cutting remark.
explanation.definitionFit: A barb is a pointed, wounding remark, the same thing as a jibe.

clue.text: Perhaps a plus for someone in the theatre?

blocks.note: first meaning: a mathematical symbol such as plus or minus
second meaning: a surgeon working in an operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: The theatre sounds like the stage, and a plus like an asset to a cast; it is the hospital operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: In maths a symbol like + is called an operator, and a surgeon who operates is also an operator.

clue.text: Minister, say, in council losing heart? Idle, perhaps

indicators.note: the word loses all its inner letters, leaving only the two ends

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
Eric Idle of Monty Python's Flying Circus

explanation.surface: A church minister on the council is losing enthusiasm and growing lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Idle looks like an adjective for the minister, but it is the surname of the comedian Eric Idle, so 'perhaps' marks Eric as one example of an Idle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric is a member of the clergy, and a minister of religion is one example of that.

clue.text: Seven plus nine minus indefinite number confused Freud, say

indicators.note: minus means take away, so one letter is subtracted from the combined words
confused letters are jumbled out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
n is the algebra symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Arithmetic so muddled that it would baffle Sigmund Freud.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one N from SEVEN plus NINE and rearrange the eight letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigmund Freud lived and worked in Vienna, so he is an example of a Viennese person.

clue.text: A geezer tucked into large drink somewhere in Spain

indicators.note: something tucked into another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large
a geezer is slang for a man
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A bloke squeezes in to get a big drink somewhere in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A geezer is British slang for a man, and cha (or char) is British slang for tea; A MAN goes between L and CHA.
explanation.definitionFit: La Mancha is a region of central Spain, famous as Don Quixote's homeland.

clue.text: One's next to hip rock-'n'-roller on piano

blocks.note: p is the musical marking for piano, softly
Elvis Presley, the king of rock and roll; 'on' puts him after P

explanation.surface: A hip rock-and-roll star sits beside a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hip' reads as cool, the obvious partner for a rock-'n'-roller, but the definition means the joint, and Elvis was famous for swivelling his.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelvis is the bony basin of the lower trunk, and the hip joints sit on either side of it.

clue.text: Swan around and sing quietly in German city

indicators.note: turned around, the word faces the other way and is read backwards

blocks.note: a cob is a male swan
to hum is to sing softly with closed lips

explanation.surface: A swan paddles about while someone hums in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bochum is an industrial city in the Ruhr district of western Germany.

clue.text: One famous Russell keeping secret occasionally for another famous Russell

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter is taken
keeping means holding something inside

blocks.note: the comedian Russell Brand
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: One celebrity Russell is keeping a secret for another celebrity Russell.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertrand Russell, the philosopher and logician, is the other well-known Russell, here by first name.

clue.text: Enlightenment from men in part of weekend newspaper

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the others

blocks.note: Sat is short for Saturday
OR is other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
the i is a British newspaper, a sister paper of the Independent

explanation.surface: Finding spiritual insight in the men's section of the Saturday paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The men go between SAT and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Satori is the Zen Buddhist term for sudden spiritual enlightenment.

clue.text: Sign in a bar: "Cola left to get drunk"

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pub notice telling customers that leftover cola is fair game to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is a bar of music, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The alto clef is a symbol on the stave fixing the pitch of notes, written at the start of a bar of music.

clue.text: Unease of rapper, putting out cover

indicators.note: putting out its cover removes the outside letters at each end

blocks.note: a gangsta is a gangsta rapper

explanation.surface: A rapper feels uneasy about releasing his album cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a feeling of anxiety and dread, a deep form of unease.

clue.text: Urging reforms with Bible, did special reconciliation work (in pairs of across answers here)

indicators.note: something that reforms takes a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
S is the abbreviation for special

explanation.surface: A preacher pressing for reform armed with scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme: pairs of across answers join to hide famous bridges, such as RIALTO across SATORI and ALTO CLEF, HUMBER across BOCHUM and BERTRAND, and GOLDEN GATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Building bridges is the idiom for restoring good relations between estranged parties, which is reconciliation.

clue.text: One having a wee bit of liqueur in a torpor

indicators.note: bit of means only a stretch of the following words is wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of liqueur, all of in a, and the start of torpor

explanation.surface: Someone drowsy after a small drop of liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like small, the word before bit, but it belongs to the definition as the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A urinator is a person who passes urine, which is to say having a wee.

clue.text: Rio parties hosted by terrible ruler succeeded for African countrymen

indicators.note: to party is to have a wild time, so these letters are thrown about
a guest hosted by someone is held inside their home

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
Ivan the Terrible, tsar of Russia
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Festivities in Rio laid on by a dreadful ruler, who was then replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivorians are people from Côte d'Ivoire, the Ivory Coast in West Africa.

clue.text: Starter of duck wraps, but no new spreads

indicators.note: the starter is the first letter of the next word
but no means without, so a letter is taken out

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
to envelop is to wrap up
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A menu: duck pancake wraps as a starter, but no new spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that develops grows and expands, just as something that spreads extends further.

clue.text: Thrill of breaking defensive structure

indicators.note: breaking smashes the words apart, so their letters are recombined

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The excitement of storming an enemy's defences.
explanation.definitionFit: A hill fort is an ancient earthwork fortification on a hilltop, built for defence.

clue.text: Car carrying detective's superior

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying a passenger holds them inside

blocks.note: the Lada is a Russian car make
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A police car carrying a detective's senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Superior' looks like the detective's boss, but the 's means is, and superior is an adjective for snooty.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes pretentious, affected manners, the same as being haughty and superior.

clue.text: Shelter invaded by old con

indicators.note: a place invaded by someone has them inside it

blocks.note: a haven is a refuge
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A refuge raided by an old convict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old con' reads as a former prisoner; old gives a letter and con is the verb meaning to trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone on is a British idiom for teasing or fooling them, so it means to con.

clue.text: Try hem for trousers or suit

indicators.note: a hem is the edge of a garment, so only the edge letters are kept

blocks.note: a court hears, or tries, a case
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A tailor's choice: take up the trouser hem or buy a whole new suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is one of the four suits in a pack of playing cards.

clue.text: Earl following rogue is too vain

indicators.note: rogue letters have gone astray from their proper places
following places this piece after the next one

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
E is the abbreviation for Earl

explanation.surface: A disreputable earl who is altogether too conceited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vain' suggests conceited, matching the rogue earl, but here it means futile.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no practical purpose, which is vain in the sense of useless.

clue.text: Give utilitarian philosopher grinding instrument

blocks.note: to hand something over is to give it
John Stuart Mill, the utilitarian thinker

explanation.surface: An instruction to pass a utilitarian thinker a tool for grinding.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand-mill is a small mill turned by hand, used to grind coffee, pepper or grain.

clue.text: Plaything left for Constantine I

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
ego is the Latin for I, the language of the Roman emperor Constantine

explanation.surface: A toy left behind for the first Emperor Constantine.
explanation.walkthrough: Constantine I looks like the regnal name of the emperor; read it as the word I in Constantine's Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the brand of interlocking plastic building bricks, a children's toy.

clue.text: Spaniard's cheer heard for café option?

indicators.note: heard means the word is judged by how it sounds, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: olé is the shout of a Spanish crowd at a bullfight

explanation.surface: Spanish cheering heard across a café.
explanation.definitionFit: Café au lait is coffee with milk, so au lait is a way of ordering coffee; the question mark flags the partial phrase.

clue.text: Brilliant record spun, with jazzy end

indicators.note: a spun record turns round, so the word is read backwards
jazzy means improvised and lively, so the letters are freely rearranged

blocks.note: a log is a record, as in a ship's log
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dazzling vinyl disc spinning, with a jazz finale.
explanation.definitionFit: Golden can mean excellent or outstanding, as in a golden opportunity, so it matches brilliant.

clue.text: Tech entrepreneur reduced job's entry requirement?

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: Bill Gates, co-founder of Microsoft
a post is a job

explanation.surface: A tech magnate cutting the requirements for applying to a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entry requirement' suggests job qualifications; the question mark signals a joke about a post that a gate hangs on.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatepost supports a gate, and a gate is needed to make an entrance, hence a whimsical entry requirement.
